A1.justification: While I appreciate the consensus-building process and generally support prioritizing fairness, I remain concerned about relying heavily on predictive modeling to identify ‘at-risk’ students. The conditions around data usage – particularly sensitive information - feel precarious. I would only support implementation if accompanied by robust ongoing monitoring for bias, clear student opt-out mechanisms, and significant investment in universal support services, not just targeted interventions. Transparency is critical.

A2.justification: While I support this provisional specification as a reasonable compromise reflecting group consensus, I maintain reservations about the reliance on even moderate improvements in identification justifying data inclusion or reduced explainability. Implementation should be contingent upon robust privacy safeguards, comprehensive advisor training, and ongoing student feedback mechanisms – coupled with clear opt-out options - to ensure this system truly serves student wellbeing.

A3.justification: While I support the overall direction – prioritizing fairness and limiting the use of sensitive data – I remain concerned about relying heavily on predictive modeling at all. Continuous monitoring and adaptation are essential.
